title: Solar Radiation, Heat Balance and Temperature

concepts.learning_objective: Define insolation and state the average energy received at the top of the atmosphere.
Explain how the changing earth-sun distance at aphelion and perihelion affects insolation.

topics.title: Variability, passage and spatial distribution of insolation
topics.ncert_sections: Variability of Insolation; Passage of Solar Radiation; Spatial Distribution of Insolation

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the factors that cause variation in the amount and intensity of insolation.
Describe what happens to solar radiation as it passes through the atmosphere.
Explain the pattern of insolation received at the earth's surface across latitudes.

topics.title: Heating and cooling of the atmosphere
topics.ncert_sections: Heating and Cooling of Atmosphere; Terrestrial Radiation

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how conduction heats the lower layers of the atmosphere.
Distinguish between vertical (convection) and horizontal (advection) transfer of heat.
Explain why the atmosphere is heated indirectly by long wave terrestrial radiation.

topics.title: Heat budget of the planet earth
topics.ncert_sections: Heat Budget of the Planet Earth; Variation in the Net Heat Budget

concepts.learning_objective: State the share of insolation reflected back to space as the earth's albedo.
Account for the units of energy absorbed and radiated in the earth's heat budget.
Explain the latitudinal surplus and deficit in net radiation and its redistribution.

topics.title: Temperature and factors controlling its distribution

concepts.learning_objective: Apply the normal lapse rate to estimate temperature change with altitude.
Explain how distance from the sea, air masses and ocean currents affect temperature.
Define isotherms and relate their general trend to latitude.
Compare the distribution of temperature in January and July in the two hemispheres.
Calculate and interpret the annual range of temperature.
Explain the conditions and effects of temperature inversion.
Explain air drainage and its effect in hills and valleys.
